Hemingray and American Manufactured
Aqua Teal and Clear, Vintage Mid-Century Era
This collection of three vintage glass insulators represents a significant era in American telecommunications history. Used primarily to insulate telegraph and telephone wires from their wooden support poles, these heavy glass pieces are prized by collectors for their industrial aesthetic and vibrant glass colors. This lot provides a balanced display including a classic aqua teal piece and two clear glass specimens.
Pieces Included:
Hemingray Insulator, Aqua Teal Glass, embossed "HEMINGRAY" with beaded drip points - minor base fleabites

description:
A 7-inch 45 RPM single by Kenny Rogers and the First Edition on the orange Reprise Records “Back to Back Hits” label with the riverboat logo. One side is the classic “Ruby, Don’t Take Your Love to Town,” written by Mel Tillis, produced by Jimmy Bowen, and arranged by Glen D. Hardin. The other side is the story-song favorite “Reuben James,” written by Harvey and Etris and arranged and produced by Mike Post. It comes in an olive gold Philadelphia International Records “The Sound of Philadelphia” company sleeve with the bold magenta logo. It would make a great addition to a country or country-pop 45 collection, a jukebox, or a retro music display.
Details:
Style: 7-inch 45 RPM Back to Back Hits single in a company paper sleeve
Color: Black vinyl with an orange Reprise label and riverboat logo, plus an olive gold sleeve with magenta and brown print
Size: About 7 in across (see tape measure photo)
Marks: Reprise Back to Back Hits 0738; L6669 (Ruby, Don’t Take Your Love to Town, 2:52, Spring ‘69) and M17354 (Reuben James, 2:44, Fall ‘69); Made in U.S.A.
Condition:
The record is flat and keeps a glossy finish. The vinyl has light surface scuffs and faint handling marks that show under light, plus a small mark near the label on the “Reuben James” side. Both labels are bright, with sharp, readable print and no writing or stickers. There are a few small dark specks near the center hole on the “Ruby” side. The Philadelphia International sleeve is not the original Reprise sleeve. It has light toning, soft creasing, a small white mark near one top corner, and light wear along the edges and corners. It still holds and protects the record well. Please review all photos. Sold as shown.

Corn Cob Pipe Wood Display Plaque

Original green paper label on pipe base marked Hirschl & Bendheim, Washington, Missouri
Plaque measures approximately 7.25 inches wide by 5 inches tall

Bundle in used condition, cleaned and handled
Category:

Description:
This collector's bundle features an intriguing mix of loose polished rocks, various mineral specimens, crystal clusters, and fossil fragments, providing broad appeal for geology enthusiasts and educators. Among the assortment are a striking triangular purple crystal cluster resembling amethyst, a large cream-colored crystal matrix, a long translucent white mineral specimen with fibrous striations, and a clear pointed crystal. Other notable pieces include a lustrous golden-brown banded stone, a turquoise-green mineral set on a beige matrix, a rough smaller purple cluster, and a polished gray-lavender slab with mustard veining and open cavities. Fossil interest is added by several dark triangular fragments likely fossil shark teeth, and a selection of multicolored tumbled stones in a small clear bag. All pieces are loose and suited for educational display, personal mineral collections, or hands-on learning. Surfaces range from polished and glossy to granular and rough, with no visible damage or major flaws. The bundle shows standard signs of handling and prior cleaning. An excellent introduction to the hobby of rock and mineral collecting.

Natural Petrified Wood Specimen
Agatized Fossilized Wood Display
Natural Mineral Fossil, 10.4 Inches, 2.9 lbs
Substantial natural petrified wood specimen exhibiting well-preserved exterior bark texture alongside a richly silicified interior. Petrified wood forms through permineralization, in which organic plant tissue is buried under sediment and gradually replaced by silica minerals such as chalcedony and agate over millions of years. This freestanding piece displays a varied palette of honey amber, cream, earthy brown, and dark charcoal tones, making it an impressive display piece for fossil and mineral collectors.
Silicified fossil wood with distinct exterior bark and longitudinal grain structure
Polished and natural mineralized faces with chalcedony and agate formations
Cut flat base allowing the specimen to sit upright unsupported for tabletop or shelf display
Measures 10.4 inches long by 6.4 inches wide by 3.8 inches high; weighs approximately 2.9 pounds
Condition:
Natural geological specimen in very good display condition. Features expected natural fissures, crevices, and conchoidal fractures typical of agatized wood. Flat cut base is level and stable. No synthetic coatings, glue, or modern repairs detected.

Combined Shipping Policy:
We’re happy to offer combined shipping when items meet ShopGoodwill’s combined-shipping eligibility criteria and can be safely packaged together.If the combined-shipping option is available at checkout, please proceed with payment and your items will be shipped together at a reduced shipping charge. If the option isn’t offered, the items must be purchased and shipped separately.
Please note: It is against our policy to override the ShopGoodwill system or create a combined shipment when the system does not allow it.
Mixing Flat-Rate & Dimensional Weight Items
When an order includes both flat-rate and dimensional-weight items, shipping may be calculated using dimensional weight. Combining these items does not necessarily reduce shipping costs and may result in the same or higher shipping charges than purchasing them separately.
For this reason, customers may want to consider purchasing flat-rate and dimensional-weight items in separate orders.
Flat-Rate Shipping
Flat-rate shipping charges are fixed and
cannot be adjusted or discounted
.
When multiple flat-rate items are purchased together, the shipping charge for each item is added to the order. For example, if three items each have a $5.99 flat-rate shipping charge, the total shipping charge will be $17.97
Shipping via FedEx:
All items will ship via FedEx. FedEx shipping charges are calculated using the dimensional weight (volume) or the actual weight of the shipped package - whichever weight is higher. The listed weight of this item(s) may reflect the dimensional shipping charge for the final package, and not the actual weight of the item(s). FedEx cannot ship to a Military Box, PO Box, or Puerto Rico. Orders with a tracking number assigned on a weekend are picked up by the carrier on Monday afternoon. Any order with items totaling $300 or more will automatically require a signature.

The assortment will enhance any decor, spark curiosity in geology, or serve as a tactile teaching aid. The items are in used condition with minor handling wear and the jade piece is missing from the display card. Overall, this bundle showcases visually striking and varied stones, suitable for display, collecting, or gifting to crystal enthusiasts. Category: Collectibles & Art

They still retain their utility and offer excellent potential for decorative, educational, or experimental uses. Whether you repurpose them for a display, utilize them in science projects, or add them to a vintage glassware collection, these tubes provide a solid and versatile option. title: Hemingray 42 Glass Insulator Set 2 Aqua Blue Green CD 154 Made in USA Vintage
description:
Hemingray Glass Company Set - 2 Pieces
Hemingray 42 (CD 154)
Aqua, Vintage Mid-Century
This set features two vintage aqua glass insulators produced by the Hemingray Glass Company, identified by the "Hemingray-42" mold mark. The No. 42 model, classified as CD 154 by collectors, was one of the most widely used designs for telephone and telegraph lines across North America during the early-to-mid 20th century. Prized for their deep aqua color and iconic industrial aesthetic, these pieces represent a significant era of American telecommunications history and are staple items for glass insulator collectors.
Pieces Included:
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Condition:
Both insulators are in good vintage condition with characteristic wear expected from outdoor utility use. The glass retains high clarity and its original vibrant aqua hue. As is common with authentic vintage insulators, there are minor fleabites and small chips along the sharp drip points on the beaded base. No large structural cracks or major damage to the wire grooves or top domes observed.
